Population/design and analysis sample: Adults aged 60–75 years; within-participant theta-plus versus non-rhythmic auditory stimulation; n=35 frozen confirmatory cohort
Neural and cognitive estimands: Frontocentral ITPC, evoked local log SNR, trial phase alignment; accuracy, correct response time, inverse efficiency, and individual inverse-efficiency benefit
Validation layers: Target engagement; acute behavior; condition-specific coupling; nested participant-held-out prediction
Supported inference and boundary: Theta-plus produced robust target engagement and faster responses. Coupling remained unresolved, and the analyzed EEG summaries did not establish incremental prediction of individual benefit. Outcomes were acute, and the sample was modest for individual differences.

Population/design and analysis sample: Healthy adults; simultaneous 36-Hz visual and 40-Hz auditory frequency tagging; n=20 (8,579 accuracy trials; 7,456 correct-response-time trials)
Neural and cognitive estimands: Aggregate 36/40-Hz ITPC and matched aggregate behavior; leave-one-trial-out phase projection; trial accuracy and correct-trial log response time
Validation layers: Matched aggregate reliability-validity; trial-state concurrent validity; leave-one-participant-out prediction
Supported inference and boundary: Aggregate ITPC was highly reliable, but matched 40-Hz validity intervals spanned both directions. One trial-state accuracy association was supported; prediction intervals crossed zero. Aggregate reliability was not transferred to the trial-state score.

Population/design and analysis sample: Autistic children, typically developing children, and unaffected siblings; 27/40-Hz auditory steady-state oddball task; n=111 for d-prime and n=109 for FSIQ
Neural and cognitive estimands: Aggregate 27/40-Hz ITPC and matched 40-Hz d-prime; central local log SNR and FSIQ
Validation layers: Matched aggregate reliability-validity; complementary feature-specific validity; participant-held-out prediction
Supported inference and boundary: 40-Hz ITPC was highly reliable, but its matched d-prime interval established neither directional validity nor equivalence. Local-SNR prediction intervals crossed zero; no treatment inference is permitted.
